thesis: Micron's 60-day surge follows company-disclosed record quarterly results and roughly $100B in binding multi-year AI/HBM supply contracts (including a new Anthropic partnership) that have sold out HBM capacity through 2026, a concrete demand-side catalyst rather than a rumor. A pending DRAM price-fixing class action alleges this same supply tightness reflects coordinated restriction rather than organic demand, but Micron denies the claims and the contracts are independently disclosed, company-specific commitments, not solely a pricing artifact. Fiscal Q4 earnings land 2026-09-30, an imminent unresolved catalyst that could move the stock either direction.
invalidation: FY Q4 (2026-09-30) results miss revenue/HBM gross-margin guidance or show the AI contract backlog shrinking, or the DRAM price-fixing case advances past the 2026-10-21 motion-to-dismiss hearing with a ruling adverse to Micron.
sources: CourtListener (Garciaguirre v. Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd., 3:26-cv-06345): https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/73532135/garciaguirre-v-samsung-electronics-co-ltd/

thesis: SpaceX beat Q2 2026 estimates (Space segment $962M vs $835M expected) and Starlink subscribers doubled to 12M, and on Sept 18 it won a $946M NASA Commercial Crew contract extension, both company-specific confirmed catalysts behind the 60-day rally. However, ~700M+ shares (about 5.3% of the float) are unlocking through September with another cliff in December, and the stock trades near 204x forward earnings, so a large chunk of the move is being offset by insider-selling pressure and stretched valuation rather than resolved by the fundamentals alone.
invalidation: A Q3 report showing Starlink subscriber growth stalling or Space segment revenue missing estimates, or sustained price weakness through the December lockup cliff despite the NASA contract, would undercut this thesis.

thesis: Intel's 60-day surge reflects a broad semiconductor-sector rally plus company actions: a $20B common-stock offering (upsized from $15B, priced Aug 12, 2026) to fund 14A/18A-P foundry nodes and AI infrastructure, and unconfirmed reports of an Apple foundry deal and an SK Hynix Ohio-fab partnership. The equity raise strengthens the balance sheet for the foundry turnaround but also diluted existing shareholders within the last 90 days, and much of the move rides broader chip-sector sentiment rather than a single confirmed catalyst.
invalidation: Foundry node (14A/18A-P) yield or customer-commitment updates disappoint at upcoming earnings, or the rumored Apple/SK Hynix deals fail to materialize, or the stock gives back gains once the broader chip-sector rally cools.

thesis: AMD hit a record high and briefly a $1 trillion market cap after OpenAI committed to deploy 6GW of AMD Instinct GPUs (1GW MI450 rollout starting H2 2026) and Oracle committed to 50,000 MI450 accelerators, both confirmed company-disclosed deals, alongside a Raymond James upgrade to Strong Buy. The rally is also amplified by a broader AI/chip-sector surge, and AMD's next quarterly earnings report falls within the coming months, an unresolved event that could confirm or undercut the demand story the stock is now pricing in.
invalidation: OpenAI or Oracle scale back or delay committed GPU deployments, AMD's upcoming quarterly earnings/guidance disappoint versus the AI-demand narrative, or data-center GPU market share losses to Nvidia widen.

thesis: Dell's Q2 FY27 report (Sep 1, 2026) beat on revenue (+58% YoY) and EPS, with a record $95B AI-server backlog and raised full-year guidance, driving the 60-day price move. A pending $70M pricing lawsuit from XTX Markets over server cost pass-throughs, with the case adjourned to a December 2026 court date, is a live but financially minor distraction relative to the backlog-driven growth story.
invalidation: A downward revision to the AI-server backlog/guidance in the next quarterly report, or an adverse December ruling/development in the XTX Markets litigation that signals broader customer pricing disputes, would undermine this thesis.

thesis: Akamai confirmed a signed 7-year, $11.6B cloud/compute deal with Anthropic (option to scale to ~$20B), disclosed 2026-09-25, driving the 9.03x volume spike and a ~15-20% intraday pop. Piper Sandler models ~$1.66B incremental ARR and raised PT to $158 from $125; Akamai confirmed 2026 revenue guidance is unchanged, and disclosed related Lenovo/Jabil compute buildout deals. Countering the bullish read: Anthropic received a warrant for up to 5% of AKAM shares as deal consideration -- a real, freshly-disclosed dilution mechanic -- and much of the good news is already priced into today's pop, raising sell-the-news risk for late entrants. No active litigation with a scheduled ruling in the next 90 days, no restatement/auditor dismissal/executive indictment in the last 3 years, and no problem-driven leadership turnover (a board member's resignation was to take an outside CEO role, unrelated to Akamai issues).
invalidation: Deal terms unwind or are renegotiated, the Anthropic warrant is exercised at scale without offsetting revenue realization, the ~$5.5B capex materially pressures margins/FCF, or AKAM gives back most of today's gain on no incremental news.

thesis: No company-specific news, earnings, M&A, analyst action, or regulatory event dated 2026-09-25 (or the prior few sessions) plausibly explains CM's 4.34x volume spike; CM's own price move was modest (~+0.4%). Confirmed recent CIBC news is routine: a CAD 1.07 dividend with a 9/28 ex-date, a tokenized-deposit interbank pilot announced 9/22, and CFO remarks at the Barclays financial services conference. The spike more likely rides a broad, well-documented 2026 rally across Canadian bank stocks (Big Six up ~30% YTD on strong sector Q3 earnings) rather than a CM-specific driver -- a sector-wide/technical move, not a company catalyst.
invalidation: A CM-specific catalyst emerges (earnings surprise, M&A, credit event, regulatory action) that explains the volume and changes the fundamental picture; or the elevated volume recurs alongside a clear directional price move, warranting re-screening.
sources: StockTitan/company IR aggregation of CIBC dividend and pilot news (2026-09-22 to 2026-09-25)
Reuters/sector coverage: Canadian Big Six bank rally 2026 (Q3 earnings season)

thesis: Select Water Solutions signed a definitive agreement (announced 2026-09-24) to acquire Pilot Water Solutions, a Delaware Basin produced-water midstream operator, for $700M ($600M cash + $100M WTTR Class A stock, +$15M contingent), expected to close Q4 2026. Management guides Pilot's adjusted EBITDA from $100-110M (2026) to $120-130M (2027) on a new 175,000 bbl/day minimum-volume contract -- a specific, signed, company-disclosed growth catalyst plausibly behind the 3.06x volume spike and ~4-5% pre-market pop. Countering the bullish case: the stock had fallen ~4.8% just two sessions earlier on valuation concerns, and closing remains subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals -- an unresolved binary that could reverse the read if delayed or renegotiated; the $100M stock component is also incremental, freshly-disclosed dilution.
invalidation: Pilot Water deal fails to close or is renegotiated on worse terms, regulatory approval is delayed past Q4 2026, or integration/leverage concerns emerge that offset the guided EBITDA accretion.

thesis: Marvell's Q2 FY27 earnings (Aug 27, 2026) showed record revenue of $2.74B (+37% YoY) with raised FY27 (~$12B) and FY28 (~$18B) revenue outlooks driven by data-center/AI demand, plus a new industry-first 2nm optical interconnect announcement reinforcing its AI-connectivity positioning. The stock's run partly anticipates the October 6, 2026 Investor Day where management is expected to detail custom-silicon targets through fiscal 2029, leaving one real near-term swing factor still unresolved.
invalidation: A weak, vague, or walked-back custom-silicon growth target at the October 6 Investor Day, or a deceleration in data-center revenue growth in the next quarterly report, would invalidate the continued-hold thesis.

thesis: NVDA's 60-day rally coincides with strong Q2 FY27 results (revenue $96.2B, +106% YoY) plus the Sept 24 US-China summit outcome in which Washington approved H200 AI chip exports to Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and other Chinese buyers, a market the company's own guidance had priced at zero. Beijing has urged domestic firms to limit purchases and Nvidia now remits 15% of China sales to the US government as a license condition, so this suggests the regulatory hurdle is cleared but actual revenue uptake is not yet confirmed.
invalidation: Chinese buyers do not materially take up H200 purchases despite approval, Beijing formally restricts the purchases, or Q3 FY27 earnings show data-center growth decelerating.

thesis: AXT posted record Q2 2026 revenue (~$47.6M) with a swing to profitability, and on Sept 21 the stock was added to the S&P SmallCap 600, a confirmed index-driven demand catalyst layered on top of the earnings result. The position remains up from the $67.48 average cost, but China export-permit delays for Tongmei's indium phosphide and other substrates are still not fully resolved, and heavy insider selling (~$78.8M over the trailing year, no purchases) alongside a stretched valuation are real offsetting factors that keep this from being a clean read.
invalidation: Renewed or expanded China export-permit denials that reimpose the shipment backlog, or a Q3 report showing the profitability swing reversing, would invalidate continuing to hold.

thesis: SK hynix's rally is underpinned by confirmed record Q2 2026 profit, a roughly 56-58% share of the global HBM market, HBM4 mass shipments started, and capacity described as essentially sold out into 2027 -- concrete, disclosed operating strength. Yet the stock fell about 9.6% on the very day it reported those record results because they missed elevated analyst expectations, showing the market is already pricing in a lot of the good news and pricing/expectations risk cuts both ways. The same DRAM price-fixing class action naming Micron also names SK hynix, with a motion-to-dismiss hearing set for 2026-10-21.
invalidation: HBM/DRAM pricing or demand shows signs of rolling over, capacity utilization or contracted backlog data weakens, or the DRAM antitrust case produces an adverse ruling or expands in scope after the 2026-10-21 hearing.
sources: CourtListener (Garciaguirre v. Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd., 3:26-cv-06345): https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/73532135/garciaguirre-v-samsung-electronics-co-ltd/

thesis: AAPL sits 1.25% below its 52-week high on already-realized iPhone 17 demand (shipments +13% YoY, global share at an all-time 21% per Counterpoint) plus anticipation of the Oct 23 foldable iPhone launch, alongside a completed, orderly CEO transition (Ternus succeeded Cook Sept 1). This suggests durable product-cycle strength, but a scheduled EU Digital Markets Act compliance deadline on Oct 1, 2026 and a reportedly imminent second EU DMA fine represent a near-term company-specific regulatory event that could pressure App Store economics.
invalidation: The EU imposes a material new DMA fine or forces disruptive App Store changes at the Oct 1 deadline, iPhone 17/18 demand data rolls over, or DOJ antitrust settlement talks break down into an adverse ruling.
